episodes.215897: Scattered shower and thunderstorms began to form ahead of a cold frontal passage in an environment that experienced ample destabilization during the late morning and afternoon hours across eastern Pennsylvania. Thunderstorm coverage initially struggled to form across western Pennsylvania due to lack of shear; however, more organized thunderstorm activity began to occur east of the Allegheny Front. Thunderstorms were initially very slow moving and would often begin training, allowing for multiple instances of flash flooding during the evening hours. Flash flooding was most notable in the Harrisburg and Lancaster metro areas; however, flooding, including a water rescue due to cars being stranded in high water was also observed near Bloomsburg. Isolated instances of tree damage were also observed across southeastern Pennsylvania, with multiple instances of tree damage in Lebanon County.
episodes.215908: Thunderstorms developed in a very unstable atmosphere. There was enough flow for storms to be moving, but some storms trained over one another, resulting in isolated flash flooding. Localized rainfall amounts of two to five inches were observed.
episodes.215911: Modest moisture combined with daytime heating underneath a strong area of high pressure resulted in thunderstorm development across the mountain ranges of New Mexico during the afternoon hours on August 28th. One storm produced heavy rainfall over the Salt burn scar in the Ruidoso area resulting in flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scar along U.S. 70.
episodes.215966: Warm temperatures and easterly upslope winds allowed isolated thunderstorms to develop on the afternoon of the 27th across the extreme southwestern Texas Panhandle. Thunderstorms were primarily pulse type storms due to strong instability and weak wind shear. One of these storms was able to produce ping pong ball size hail in rural Bailey County.
episodes.216215: A slow moving cold front produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.216220: A slow moving cold front produced heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.216594: A stalled frontal boundary across the Piedmont of central North Carolina led to the development of late afternoon and evening thunderstorms across the eastern Piedmont, Sandhills, and southern Coastal Plain. Storms weakened in intensity by the mid-evening hours, but continued to produce heavy rainfall, leading to isolated flash flood reports across Scotland County.
episodes.216595: A cold front draped along the central and southern Appalachians led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. The strongest storms tracked east-southeast across the western and southern Piedmont and Sandhills of central North Carolina, where numerous damaging wind reports were observed.
episodes.216626: A few isolated severe storms produced damage around the Huntsville Area.
episodes.216627: A few severe thunderstorms developed over portions of southeast Texas, producing damaging winds, hail and flash flooding.
episodes.217009: Pockets of heavy rain resulted in some localized flash flooding. In addition, a lightning strike resulted in a house fire.
episodes.217345: A decaying thunderstorm that developed over the Baja Spine and moved northward towards the International Border south of the Imperial Valley resulted in a strong outflow that moved northward through the Imperial Valley during the mid to late afternoon hours. Peak wind gusts reached 50-55 mph with Imperial Airport registering a peak gust of 51 mph, which was enough to result in a dust storm with visibilities reduced under a quarter mile and downed poles.
episodes.217584: Isolated flash flooding occurred on 8/27 associated with a favorable environment where precipitable values were around 2 inches within a moist and unstable air mass with MLCAPE values over 2000 J/kg. Generally weak southwesterly flow ahead of an approaching upper trough allowed for training of convection with high rain rates.
episodes.217751: After a warm front lifted north of the area early in the day, enough clearing occurred to allow for showers and isolated thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon and evening well ahead of an approaching cold front. Rainfall was locally heavy which led to several streets flooding and water getting into a few basements.
episodes.217754: After a warm front lifted north of the area early in the day, enough clearing occurred to allow for showers and isolated thunderstorms to develop during the afternoon and evening well ahead of an approaching cold front. Locally heavy rainfall led to an isolated instance of street flooding near Veterans Stadium.
episodes.217822: On August 28th, a strong thunderstorm moves across eastern St. Johns County in northeast Florida, acquiring weak rotation while moving across the slow moving sea breeze by the coast, and therefore producing a brief waterspout just to the northeast of Vilano Beach, FL.
episodes.217884: Two days worth (27th and 28th) of southwesterly flow aloft was capped with an upper level low traversing the region on the 29th with a cold front. While none of the three days were particularly impressive from a setup perspective (Lacking one or more of forcing, thermodynamics, or kinematics), that did not stop the thunderstorms that formed from producing isolated severe reports.
episodes.217972: A thunderstorm complex in central Nebraska moved south through southwestern Nebraska, and eventually into northwest Kansas, producing a peak 77 mph wind gust.
episodes.217973: A thunderstorm complex in central Nebraska moved south through southwestern Nebraska, and eventually into northwest Kansas, producing up to 1 inch hail and up to 60 mph wind gusts.
episodes.218110: A few strong to severe storms developed over the northern Victoria Crossroads, primarily impacting Victoria County August 28th. Hail less than an inch was observed with wind speeds generally sub-severe. One mesonet station did report a wind gust of severe strength, at 58 mph.
episodes.218214: Deep moisture, weak shear and ample instability supported slow moving showers and   thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall and flash flooding, especially across parts of Beaufort and Hampton Counties in the Yemassee area. A COOP Observer located in Yemassee reported a 24-hour rainfall amount of 10 inches, most of which occurred between 2 PM to 830 PM.
episodes.218225: A weak frontal boundary slowing dropping southward into southern Georgia was the main driving force behind scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms, including isolated strong to severe thunderstorms during this period, along with the usual interactions with sea breeze/outflow interactions during strong diurnal heating. Many areas received 2+ inches or more of rainfall during this period thanks to very high available moisture and slow storm motion, though a report of isolated severe thunderstorm damage also occurred with this episode.
episodes.218307: Ample instability but not much flow aloft led to scattered slow-moving storms with heavy rainfall.
episodes.218308: Ample instability but not much flow aloft led to scattered slow-moving storms with heavy rainfall.
episodes.218309: Ample instability but not much flow aloft led to scattered slow-moving storms with gusty winds and a waterspout.
episodes.218325: A warm front passed through the region in the morning hours of Thursday, August 27th, 2026, placing eastern New York within the warm sector of a surface cyclone translating eastward from southeast Ontario into southwest Quebec. A surface trough propagating through the warm sector ahead of the main cold front forced the development of scattered thunderstorms, some of which became severe, that afternoon and evening. The most notable storms occurred in the Upper-Hudson Valley, specifically in Saratoga County, where two weak tornadoes eventually formed. The first, an EF-1 in Wilton, snapped and uprooted numerous softwood and hardwood trees during its 4 minute, 1.22 mile track. The second, an EF-0, uprooted several softwood trees near Ruggles Road and Preserve Way. The storm which spawned the tornadoes caused a fair amount of wind damage itself, mainly in the town of Wilton but outside of the 250 yard tornado width. ||A few other severe storms developed in Ulster and Herkimer Counties, leading to additional tree and wire damage near Shandaken, Napanoch, and Cold Brook. A third weak tornado also developed in southwest Hamilton County as the aforementioned severe storm in Herkimer crossed into its border. This was another very brief EF-0 which caused numerous softwood trees to snap and become uprooted in a remote area of the Adirondacks.
episodes.218460: Had thunderstorm winds gusts reach severe speeds and cause damage as well.
episodes.218480: With the subtropical ridge remaining in place, a stronger trough would impact the Pacific Northwest resulting in more widespread flash flooding across southern and central Utah, as well as widespread severe weather across the majority of Utah. This would go on to produce a prolific wind-driven hail event in Lynndyl, Utah.
episodes.218512: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina throughout the afternoon. Several storms produced locally damaging wind gusts across the Piedmont and foothills.
episodes.218516: Isolated thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced locally damaging wind gusts in Greenville County.
episodes.218580: Monsoon moisture resulted in an isolated thunderstorm in Clark County in southern Nevada that produced severe winds.
